# Judith Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_016_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Judith said, Begin to my God with timbrels, sing to my Lord with cymbals; strike up for him a new psalm, exalt and call upon his name.

**2** For the LORD is a God who crushes wars; he has set up his camp among his people; he delivered me from the hand of those who pursued me.

**3** Assur came from the mountains of the north; he came with ten thousands of his army; their multitude stopped up the wadis, and their cavalry covered the hills.

**4** He said he would set fire to my territory and kill my young men with the sword, and dash my infants to the ground, and give my children as prey, and take my virgins as spoil.

**5** The Lord Almighty brought them to nothing by the hand of a female.

**6** For their mighty one did not fall by the hand of young men, nor did the sons of Titans strike him down, nor did tall giants set upon him; but Judith daughter of Merari undid him with the beauty of her face.

**7** For she put off the garb of her widowhood to exalt the afflicted in Israel; she anointed her face with oil of myrrh,

**8** and she bound up her hair in a tiara, and she put on a linen garment to deceive him.

**9** Her sandal ravished his eye, and her beauty captured his soul, and the sword passed through his neck.

**10** The Persians trembled at her boldness, and the Medes were confounded at her daring.

**11** Then the wretched ones shouted and my oppressed ones cried out; the enemy was frightened; they screamed and fled.

**12** The sons of girls who pierced them through, and the sons of the deserters struck them; they perished before the face of the Lord my God.

**13** I will sing to my God a new song: O Lord, great and glorious are you, wondrous in strength, invincible.

**14** Let all your creation serve you, for you spoke and they were made; you sent forth your breath and it built them up; and no one can resist your voice.

**15** For mountains together with waters will be shaken from their foundations, and rocks will melt like wax before your face; but to those who fear you you will be merciful.

**16** For a small thing is a sacrifice of pleasant odor, and less than fat offered as a whole burnt offering for you; but the one who fears the Lord is great forever.

**17** Woe to the nations that rise up against my people — the Lord Almighty will punish them on the day of judgment; he will send fire and worms into their flesh, and they will weep in pain forever.

**18** Now when they came to Jerusalem, they worshiped God. And when the people were purified, they offered their whole burnt offerings and their freewill offerings and their gifts.

**19** And Judith dedicated to God all the possessions of Holofernes which the people had given her, and the canopy which she had taken from his bedchamber she gave as a devoted thing.

**20** And the people continued to make merry in Jerusalem before the sanctuary for three months, and Judith remained with them.

**21** After these days every man went away to his own inheritance, and Judith went to Bethulia and remained on her own estate; and in her time she became famous throughout all the land of Israel.

**22** And many men desired her, but no man knew her all the days of her life from the day that her husband Manasseh died and was gathered to his people.

**23** And she grew ever more famous, and she grew old in her husband's house, reaching one hundred and five years. And she gave her maidservant her freedom. And she died in Bethulia, and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasseh.

**24** And the house of Israel mourned her for seven days. And before she died she distributed her property to all those who were nearest to Manasseh her husband and to those nearest to her own family.

**25** And no one ever spread fear among the sons of Israel again in the days of Judith, and for many days after her death.

---
*EMET notes: The song (vv. 1-17) alternates between praise (1-2), historical narrative (3-12), and doxology (13-17). v. 5 — "female" (thēleia) rather than "woman" (gynē) — the choice is deliberate and more pointed in Greek; it emphasizes the category, not the person. v. 6 — "sons of Titans" (Titanes) — Greek mythological giants representing supreme earthly power; the author uses Hellenistic language to say no human force could have done what Judith did. v. 9 — "ravished his eye... captured his soul" — beauty as weapon, perfectly engineered. v. 14 — "sent forth your breath" echoes Genesis 2:7 and Psalm 104:30. v. 25 — the book's final verse is the epitaph.*
